_doc: COMPOSED ENDINGS (Steve 2026-10-14 round 5, on path final + one build coda: "Nope good idea that's kinda manageable."). An ending = the Table path's own light/dark final (table-<path>.js, never in this file) + ONE build coda. codas.<selector> = { light: [lines], dark: [lines] }, path-independent; selectors 'god:<godId>' (10), 'class:<path>/<subclass>' (20), 'track:<track>' (5) = 70 codas. The most specific coda for the locked ending key plays: god > class/subclass > track; none = the final alone. The relay's grey band reads light or dark by relayLean (>0 light, <0 dark, 0 light), the same rule as its door gift. paths.<tablePath>.<selector>.<moral> = { title?, lines, finals?: { <finalId>: [lines that REPLACE that final's outcome] } } is a RARE BESPOKE OVERRIDE and wins over every coda (lookup god > class/subclass > class > track; morals light, dark, grey on the relay; final ids per table-<path>.js plus 'hosts' and 'poddemand', which add lines only). Tokens: {name} {class} {god} {verb} {path} (the Table path's name, e.g. 'the Beloved'). Voice: spare, second person, two lines. Validate and list what's missing: node scripts/validate-table-endings.js --todo

codas._doc: One build coda per selector x moral, played after the path's final. Exemplars 2026-10-14: god:one_person_army, class:caregiver/keeper, track:combat.

light: The System called you {god}. You never wanted an army. You wanted everyone home, and every wound you took, you gave back once, and then you put it down.
You kept no trophies. When the children asked what it was like to be an army, you told them: tired, and never alone.
dark: The System called you {god}, and you kept the name. Every wound since the first day had a place on your books. You kept collecting.
You brought that account to the Table. In Haven, people had learned to step aside when you passed, without knowing they were doing it.

light: You carried the keepsakes of the dead the whole way to the Table: a button, a whistle, a name scratched into a spoon. You kept finding room for one more.
The Codex kept what the dead knew. You kept the rest: who they were at dinner.
dark: You carried the dead the whole way to the Table and made them stand behind you while you talked. The table counted them as yours. You let it.
You had kept setting places for people who were not coming. Nobody in Haven had dared to sit in them.

light: You came to the Table as {path} the hard way: one fight at a time, most of them for someone else.
Before dawn, you had walked the fence again. It was a good fence. You knew it did not need walking. You had needed to make sure.
dark: You came to the Table as {path} the hard way, and you made sure the hard way went through everyone in front of you.
Before dawn, you had woken with a hand on the knife. Haven slept fine. You had learned not to ask why.

light: You learned how much a body could take. What mattered was the breathing room behind you, where someone else could lower their hands.
You did not make pain holy. You made it possible for another person to stop being brave.
dark: You took their wounds and kept an account. Every scar became a reason they should listen when you spoke.
You called it protection. The people behind you learned to ask permission before stepping out.

light: You could choose the terms. You learned to leave a way out, even for something that had come to kill you.
You kept a hunter's patience even when there was no need to wait. A trail could go cold without becoming a failure.
dark: You chose the ground, the distance, the moment. Before long, every other living thing was part of the approach.
Every movement had become a sign. You never found a word for a world with nothing left to hunt.

light: You heard the dead answer. You kept their names separate from what you needed them to do.
In every story you told about them, you left room for the things they would have refused.
dark: You heard the dead answer and mistook the answer for consent. Their silence had been easier to work with.
You spoke for all of them, including the ones who had once told you no.

light: You learned to step out of reach. You used the space it bought to make room for people who could not follow.
You only needed one place where a hand reaching for yours could find it.
dark: You learned to step out of reach. Other people kept having to stay where the consequences landed.
You could leave any room. You made that fact the last word in every argument.

light: You could see the lie before it was spoken. You learned that knowing the truth did not make every confidence yours to tell.
A folded letter was still a folded letter. You had learned enough to leave some things closed.
dark: You could see the lie before it was spoken. Soon, an unasked question felt like evidence being withheld.
You gave everyone the long, exhausting work of proving they had nothing to hide.

light: When you spoke, people heard you. You spent some of that silence waiting for an answer.
The best answer was sometimes a voice you had not expected to hear. You left the channel open.
dark: When you spoke, people heard you. After a while, you stopped leaving time for anything else.
You learned to make a crowd sound like one voice. You called the voice theirs.

light: You came back from the fire carrying the memory of its heat. You did not ask anyone else to prove they could do the same.
An ordinary meal, a dry blanket, a place to sleep: you kept finding reasons that one more day was worth the trouble.
dark: You came back from the fire and began to measure other people by what they could survive. It was a convenient measure.
You had made survival look impossible. You used that fact to end conversations about what it cost.

light: You could name a price and have it heard. You learned which things lost their meaning the moment you tried.
In the margin of your accounts, you kept a column for gifts. Nothing beside it waited to be repaid.
dark: You could name a price and have it heard. A refusal only meant you had not found the right currency yet.
You had found a way to make owing you feel like being saved.

light: You fed other mouths with what passed through your hands. Your own bowl still needed filling. You let someone do it.
You knew the harvest belonged to more than the person who could call it. Someone else was allowed to hold the serving spoon.
dark: You fed other mouths with what passed through your hands. You learned how quiet a room became when you stopped.
You kept the gate, and the list of names allowed inside.

light: You found a use for your anger that left someone else a chance to breathe. It still frightened you sometimes.
After the shouting, you had learned to listen for the answer. Your hands could shake without closing.
dark: You found a use for your anger, then found reasons to keep using it. People got good at staying out of the way.
You had begun to mistake the quiet after it for agreement.

light: You learned to take the next blow. You learned to notice when the person beside you could not.
When somebody called you unstoppable, you still thought about where to stop.
dark: You learned to take the next blow and made endurance the price of being heard. Anyone could speak, if they lasted.
You stopped looking closely at what was underfoot.

light: You held the line long enough for other people to make their own choices. Some chose to leave it.
From where you stood, the door was easy to miss. You kept checking that it still opened.
dark: You held the line until the people behind it forgot there had ever been another direction. You preferred them safe.
You had learned how little a wall had to move to become a cage.

light: You changed the ground so that someone smaller could stand on it. You marked the dangerous places where everyone could see.
You put the safe path where another person could see it. They did not have to follow your footprints exactly.
dark: You changed the ground and kept the safe route to yourself. People learned to watch your feet.
You had made being welcome a matter of staying where you were put.

light: You learned to wait until a shot was worth taking. Sometimes that meant lowering the weapon.
The arrow left in your quiver mattered too. You had not spent every clean line of sight.
dark: You learned to wait until a shot was worth taking. You began to think of every hesitation as wasted distance.
You knew too much about where everyone stood when they thought they were alone.

light: You learned the signs that meant follow, and the ones that meant enough. Your companions were more than another set of teeth.
You made room beside your own footsteps for a pace that was not yours.
dark: You learned which signs would bring the teeth running. A creature that hesitated became a problem with its training.
You stopped counting the tracks that led out and did not lead back.

light: You learned to put your hands where the hurt was. You kept listening when the hurt was something you could not mend.
Sometimes you could only stay beside the bed. You learned to stop calling that nothing.
dark: You learned to put your hands where the hurt was. You learned how grateful people could be for a little relief.
You had begun to hear a debt in every thank-you.

light: You learned to get out of reach. You kept turning back to see who needed the room you had made.
You had not forgotten what it felt like to be the person left waiting.
dark: You learned to get out of reach. Explanations became something for the people who had to stay.
You had made absence do the work of an answer.

light: You changed who stood where, and who had a chance to get away. You learned to tell the joke without choosing a victim.
You kept an honest account of who paid for the surprise. A laugh was not enough to settle it.
dark: You changed who stood where. Someone else was usually there when the blow arrived.
You had grown fond of saying that nobody should have fallen for it.

light: You saw trouble coming and gave people time to choose. You did not confuse a warning with an order.
You kept a place in your plans for being surprised by someone you loved.
dark: You saw trouble coming and began to call every other choice a mistake. It saved you a great deal of listening.
You had made the future small enough that only your answer would fit.

light: You put the crossings on the map, and the hard climbs, and the places where somebody had offered water.
You put the landmarks where another hand could copy them. A map did not have to come with its maker.
dark: You put the crossings on your map and left them off the copies. People thanked you for knowing the way.
You had made getting lost part of the price of leaving you.

light: You learned where to put the light so that a quiet person could be seen. You learned when to turn it off.
You left the people in the picture something that belonged to them when the watching stopped.
dark: You learned where to put the light. Soon, people were arranging their grief so that it would fall inside it.
You had begun to call the parts you could not use a waste.

light: You learned to make a room move together. You left enough quiet for someone at the back to disagree.
A voice at the back could still change the plan. You had kept that much space in the room.
dark: You learned to make a room move together. You learned to hear hesitation before anybody else could.
You had made standing still feel like betrayal.

light: You made a fire of yourself, and the fire still needed feeding. You learned to ask before taking the last helping.
You remembered the hands that gathered the fuel. Even the hottest body needed somebody to bring it dinner.
dark: You made a fire of yourself. A hungry body was such a persuasive reason to take a little more.
You had started to think of other people's dinner as power you had not used yet.

light: You learned how to get through one more night. You stopped asking the people beside you to promise more than that.
You kept the memory of every hand that had helped your life hold.
dark: You learned how to get through one more night. You began to treat everyone who could not as someone who had given up.
You had found a way to make needing help sound like weakness.

light: You kept things for the day they would be needed. You learned to recognize that day when somebody knocked.
You kept a key where another hand could reach it. A full store did not need an empty doorstep.
dark: You kept things for the day they would be needed. Somehow, the people asking were always a little too early.
You had become very good at counting food without counting mouths.

light: You learned to make an offer worth accepting. You left the other person a way to turn it down.
You knew the difference between a fair price and a desperate customer. You left room between the two.
dark: You learned to make an offer nobody could refuse. Hunger made the wording much easier.
You had learned to call a closed door a negotiating position.

light: You learned to tend what would feed people after your hands were busy elsewhere. You showed someone how.
You had left enough seed for a season you might not see.
dark: You learned to tend what would feed people. You made sure they knew whose hands had done it.
You had made every harvest an argument for keeping you in charge.

light: You made a meal large enough for another place. You learned the names of the people who kept finding one.
You kept the welcome larger than the price of a plate.
dark: You made a meal large enough for everyone to notice who had not been invited. The empty places did useful work.
You had learned how much obedience could fit inside a helping.

light: You learned to read the ground and to leave some of its answers where they grew. Another hungry person would come this way.
You remembered the weather, the small signs, the water found before it was too late. You passed the directions on.
dark: You learned to read the ground and took what you could before anyone else reached it. A bare patch was evidence of work.
You had left very little for the person following your tracks.

light: You learned how much could change when someone was heard all the way through. You did the difficult part and waited.
You kept the pauses where another person had found their own words.
dark: You learned how much people would tell you if you waited. You kept the useful parts.
You had found a way to make listening feel like ownership.

light: You learned to make what people needed from what was left. You showed the next pair of hands where yours had gone wrong.
A worn seam, a working hinge: you knew how much of a life could depend on something small holding.
dark: You learned to make what people needed. You left the difficult step out when someone asked to learn.
You had made yourself harder to replace than anything you built.

light: You kept looking at the thing that did not fit. You learned to bring someone with you before finding out what it could do.
The answer changed what you could do. You kept asking what you should.
dark: You kept looking at the thing that did not fit. You learned how much easier the experiment was when someone else stood closer.
You kept careful notes on what happened. The names took too much space.

light.title: THE SHOWRUNNER'S FINALE

audience: You hand the audience the microphone and walk off your own stage. It's the best cue you ever called. Trillions of viewers find out what it's like to be asked, and the show becomes the government without anyone quite deciding it should.
It works because you built it to work: every segment has an exit, every host has a replacement, and nobody holds the remote for long. The ratings dip. The constitution doesn't.
quiet: You spend the finale on people the show never booked. You give the unfilmed villages the good lighting. You give the dead the long shot. You give the quiet ones the last word, and you cut the music so it's the only sound.
The audience weeps in eleven dimensions. Nobody can find you in the footage. That was the point.

lines: Later, the galaxy will try to name the producer of the most-watched night in its history. The credits roll for an hour and list everyone in Haven, alphabetically. Your name is in there somewhere, between a beekeeper and a child.
{name} never takes a bow. At the fire that night, someone asks who ran the whole thing. Everyone looks at everyone else, and laughs, and that's the right answer.

dark.title: THE SHOWRUNNER'S CUT

audience: The audience speaks, and every word is one you wrote for it. You built the show so well that the galaxy can't tell the difference between being heard and being produced. Neither can you, most nights.
The government is a program now. You are its showrunner, uncredited and permanent. The ratings never dip. You made sure.
contract: The network slides the forever-contract across the light, and you read it twice, and you strike out the part where they own you, and you add a part where you own them. They sign. They have seen what you do to a room.
The show never ends. You never appear in it. Every cut in the galaxy goes through your hands, and somewhere in Haven a grandmother watches herself cry on a screen and doesn't remember crying.

lines: The galaxy loves Haven perfectly. Haven isn't sure which parts of itself were real.
{name} watches the final cut alone in the control room. It's flawless. You are not in a single frame of it, and that was always the job.

light.title: THE DOORWAY

walk: Humanity walks, and you walk last. Not to lead. To stand in the doorway until the last child is through, the way you stood in front of every thing that ever came for Haven. Nothing comes. The table watches you watch it, and doesn't move.
The long shot is famous: the small figures leaving the light, and one of them turned around, facing the ring, walking backwards the whole way out.
terms: You name terms like someone who has been hit before and got up: plainly, without hurry. They can have trade. They can have visits. They cannot have anyone, ever. They sign. Nobody at the ring wants to find out what you do when a promise breaks.

lines: The System named you a brawler. It never quite understood that most of the fighting was standing still in the right place.
{name} still sleeps nearest the door. Haven never asks why. Haven sleeps fine.

dark.title: THE SALTED ROAD

walk: Humanity walks, and you make sure the table remembers the walk. The collector you broke is still holding its hand. The road behind you is salt and ash and the marks of your knuckles on the light.
The long shot is famous for a different reason: the figure at the back, turning once, and every face around the ring looking away first.
terms: You name your terms with blood still on your hands, and you don't wipe them first. Everything, on your word, or you come back. They sign before you finish the sentence.

lines: The galaxy learns the other meaning of 'no': the one that hits back. The table never prices humanity again. It never invites it again either.
{name} walks home through a village that loves them and flinches when they raise a hand to wave.
